chunks: Abu Basir narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, that he said:

"Bilal was a righteous servant, and he said: 'I will not give the adhan for anyone after the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family.' So from that day, 'Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal' was left out."

key_terms.أُؤَذِّنُ: I call the adhan; I make the call to prayer
key_terms.بِلَالًا: Bilal, the well-known mu'adhdhin of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.تُرِكَ: it was left out or omitted
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ: the adhan phrase meaning 'hasten to the best of deeds'
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.عَبْدًا صَالِحًا: a righteous servant; a person of piety and uprightness

ai.seo_question: Why was "Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal" left out of the adhan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Bilal, described as a righteous servant, refused to call the adhan for anyone after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. As a result, the phrase "Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal" was left aside from that time, highlighting an early historical development connected to the adhan.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.872 - Abu Basir narrated from one of the Imams (as) that He said:

"Bilal was a righteous servant who said:
'I will not call the adhan for anyone after the Messenger of Allah (sw).'
Therefore, on that day, 'Hayya 'ala khayr al-'Amal' (Hasten to the best of deeds) was left out."
